snippet.title: What Happens When You Take Creatine
snippet.description:
What happens when you take creatine? Almost all of it is absorbed, and about 95% of the body's creatine is stored in the muscles, where it helps recharge their energy (ATP) in short, hard efforts. A review of 100 studies found small gains, mostly in short, repeated efforts, not in running or swimming. In the first days the scale can go up 1 to 3 kg, mostly water. Creatine raises creatinine on a blood test (by about 0.14 mg/dL in two 2026 reviews), which can look like kidney trouble; trials in healthy adults found no kidney harm, but that is not proof of safety for everyone.

Sources:
• Kreider RB et al. International Society of Sports Nutrition position stand: safety and efficacy of creatine supplementation in exercise, sport, and medicine. J Int Soc Sports Nutr 2017;14:18: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28615996/
• Antonio J et al. Common questions and misconceptions about creatine supplementation: what does the scientific evidence really show? J Int Soc Sports Nutr 2021;18:13: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33557850/
• Branch JD. Effect of creatine supplementation on body composition and performance: a meta-analysis. Int J Sport Nutr Exerc Metab 2003;13:198-226: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/12945830/
• Raihan FA, Supriyanta A. Creatine supplementation and kidney function in healthy, physically active adults: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Int Urol Nephrol, 17 Nov 2026: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/43050022/
• de Souza Almeida A et al. Impact of creatine supplementation on kidney health: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Int Urol Nephrol 2026;58:5423-34: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42507286/
• Lak M et al. Does creatine cause hair loss? A 12-week randomized controlled trial. J Int Soc Sports Nutr 2025: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40265319/
